samples.claim: validate first rejects every nonfinite f64 field, in order initial,min,max,decrease,increment,threshold, with InvalidInput naming field/value. Comments explain that NaN evades comparisons and can disable a downstream token bucket or panic duration conversion; those downstream behaviors are rationale, not code implemented here. NaN and infinities are rejected even for the optional maximum ceiling; finite zero disables it.

102 |     /// Validate that the configuration values are sensible.
103 |     pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<()> {
104 |         // Reject NaN and infinity first. The sign and ordering checks below
105 |         // compare with `<`/`>`, which are `false` for NaN and for a `+inf` on
106 |         // a field with no opposing bound, so a non-finite rate would otherwise
107 |         // slip through and silently disable throttling (a NaN rate makes the
108 |         // token bucket refill to full on every acquire) or, with a zero burst
109 |         // capacity, panic in `Duration::from_secs_f64`.

samples.claim: Every feature/bugfix requires tests. Local cases target under one second with small fixtures and split matrices, never weakened assertions/recall. Parameterize input-only differences with named rstest cases or pytest.parametrize; assert rather than print; extend existing tests; skipped tests require issue URLs. Dataset tests include multiple fragments; index cases cover null items/all-null/empty/null columns; vector creation must assert recall >=0.5. Compatibility fixtures live in test_data with datagen.py asserting writer version and copy_test_data_to_tmp for reads.
samples.evidence:
80 | ## Testing Standards
81 | 
82 | - **All bugfixes and features must have corresponding tests. We do not merge code without tests.**
83 | - Keep local unit tests lightweight: each test case should finish within one second on typical developer hardware. Split independent parameter matrices and use the smallest fixture or model that preserves the asserted behavior; do not relax assertions, coverage, or recall thresholds to meet the budget.
84 | - Use `rstest` (Rust) or `@pytest.mark.parametrize` (Python) for tests that differ only in inputs. Use `#[case::{name}(...)]` for readable case names.
85 | - Replace `print()` in tests with `assert` — prints don't catch regressions.
86 | - Extend existing tests instead of adding overlapping new ones. Add to existing test files.
87 | - Link a GitHub issue when skipping a test — never bare `@pytest.mark.skip` or `@Ignore` without a tracking URL.
88 | - Include multi-fragment scenarios for dataset operations (reads, indexes, scans).
89 | - Cover NULL edge cases in index tests: null items, all-null collections, empty collections, null columns.
90 | - Vector index tests must assert recall metrics (>=0.5 threshold), not just verify creation succeeds.
91 | - For backwards compatibility, use the `test_data` directory with checked-in datasets from older versions. Include a `datagen.py` that asserts the Lance version used. Use `copy_test_data_to_tmp` to read this data.
samples.review_note: Matches all contributor test requirements without execution claims.
